claims.statement: Docker Hub push/pull rate limits affect self-hosted jobs; source claims hosted-runner exemption by GitHub/Docker agreement. Pinned claim is not current external rate-limit verification.
Example routes a push job to any available build-runners member, then checkout, Node14 and bats installation/version. Group and runtime values are examples; commands/includes not executed or trusted.

Combining group and label requires both to match; example uses ubuntu-runners and ubuntu-24.04-16core with Node14/bats. It is conjunctive selection, not proof of native group permissions or actual runners.
Three OS values times three versions generate nine combinations plus include windows/version17 yields ten jobs, not ten plus one.
With no base variables, include-only configurations each generate a job; production/site-a and staging/site-b example yields two. Deployment labels are illustrative, not authorized targets.

Two OS by two Node versions yields four jobs; include adds npm6 to the matching Windows/Node16 configuration without creating another combination. Matrix-selected setup and conditional npm installation are inert examples.

Job-specific permissions modify default GITHUB_TOKEN rights to minimum required access, allowing different rights by job or workflow-level assignment. Effective organization constraints remain separately evaluated.
Workflow permissions apply globally or per job to all token-using actions/run commands within that job; organization and conditionally enterprise owners can restrict repository write access.

Source describes pull_request_target granting read/write repository token even for public forks, a critical exception to fork read-only assumptions. Explicit permission and parent policy interaction still needs review; permission table is included separately.

Job outputs map values for dependent downstream jobs via needs; expressions evaluate at job end, secret-bearing outputs are redacted and not sent, and skipped secret output produces warning. Output-limitations include and masking guidance remain separate.
Example maps step hello/world GITHUB_OUTPUT values to job outputs and consumes via needs/env; outputs are illustrative, not acquired execution evidence.

Matrix outputs combine across jobs; unique output names are required because job order is not guaranteed and the last-running matrix job overwrites colliding names. Example versions1–3 names each output distinctly.

Container credentials example references shared registry guidance and sets ghcr.io/owner/image with github.actor username and secrets.github_token password. No credential acquisition or permission sufficiency verified.
container.env sets a map of container environment variables, not a list; actual values and source trust require parent review.
container.image names Docker Hub or registry image, with separate rate-limit reusable. Registry/image name is not an immutable digest or reviewed provenance.
container.options passes additional Docker creation/resource options, but --network and --entrypoint are unsupported. Linked Docker options are not universally supported by Actions.
container.ports is an array of exposed ports, distinct from proof of host connectivity or firewall approval.

container.volumes accepts named/anonymous Docker volumes or host bind mounts for data sharing. Source is a volume name or absolute host path; destination is absolute container path; examples include anonymous /data/my_data and named/bind forms. Mounts are not approved host access.

Job container handles steps without their own container; container actions become siblings sharing network/mounts. Without job container, steps run on runs-on host except container actions. Default run shell inside container is sh, overridable at job/step scope.
Example push/main job uses Node18, development env, port80, named volume and CPU1; dockerenv probe is illustrative. String container: node:18 shorthand may omit image key; no Docker execution occurs.

fail-fast defaults true across the whole matrix; continue-on-error applies per job. Matrix jobs failing without continue-on-error cancel queued/in-progress siblings, whereas allowed experimental failures leave others running.

Four-job example combines versions6–8/nonexperimental plus included version9/experimental, with fail-fast true and per-job experimental continue-on-error. Not evidence of all tests completing or passing.

Job concurrency uses string/expression group and supports github, inputs, vars, needs, strategy and matrix; workflow-level counterpart exists. Detailed group cancellation/queue include requires separate resolution.
Workflow concurrency permits github, inputs and vars contexts only, narrower than job concurrency; group details include and job counterpart are separate.
Job if conditional is evaluated before matrix application; supported-context and expression syntax reusables do not authorize matrix-context use at this pre-matrix stage.

Example permits production-deploy only for exact octo-org/octo-repo-prod identity and otherwise marks job skipped; sample checkout/Node14/bats is not deployment proof or local approved repository policy.

Environment may be name or name/url object; URL maps to deployment API environment_url. All deployment protection rules must pass before sending its job to runner, but declaring a name is not proof of rules configured or verified.

Environment URL supports github, inputs, vars, needs, strategy, matrix, job, runner, env and steps; name permits only github, inputs, vars, needs, strategy and matrix. Output-as-URL example does not grant steps context for name.

Conditional environment-without-deployment supports deployment:false for secrets/variables without deployment object, incompatible with custom deployment rules. This qualifies the separately reviewed unconditional deployment-object fragment; branch feature availability and native policy remain unresolved.
